lesson.title: Stories and Poems
lesson.summary: A folk tale, beginning, middle and end, predicting the ending, rhymes and rhythm, and writing four lines.
learning_objectives: Retell a story in order: beginning, middle and end
Predict what happens next using clues
Spot rhymes and rhythm in a poem

standards.text: Discuss the sequence of events, make predictions, and recite poems with rhyme and rhythm

success_criteria: I can tell the beginning, middle and end of a story

blocks.markdown:
Today's big question: how do stories and poems work?

We will read, predict, rhyme and write.
blocks.say: Welcome back, story explorer! Today's big question: how do stories and poems work, and how can we make our own? We will hear an old tale, guess what happens next, play with rhymes, and write four lines. Let's go!

blocks.alt: Stories and poems are full of surprises.
blocks.caption: Stories and poems are full of surprises.

terms.meaning: A tale about characters and what happens to them.

sub_lessons.title: A folk tale: beginning, middle and end

blocks.text: Stop 1: The three parts of a story

blocks.markdown:
Every story has a **beginning**, a **middle** and an **end**.

Beginning: meet the characters. Middle: the problem. End: it is solved.
blocks.say: Every story has three parts. The beginning is where we meet the characters and the place. The middle is where the problem happens and the characters try to fix it. The end is where the problem is solved. Think of a sandwich: bread, filling, bread. Let's hear an old tale, The Thirsty Crow, and spot the three parts.

scenes.caption: Beginning: a thirsty crow finds a jug.
scenes.say: The beginning. A hot day. A crow is very thirsty. He finds a jug with only a little water at the bottom.

scenes.caption: Middle: he drops in pebbles.
scenes.say: The middle. The crow cannot reach the water. He has a clever idea. He drops pebbles into the jug, one by one.

scenes.caption: End: the crow drinks.
scenes.say: The end. The water rises to the top. The crow drinks and is happy. His clever idea solved the problem.

question.prompt: In The Thirsty Crow, what is the problem in the middle?
question.explanation: The water is too low for the crow to reach.

options.text: The crow cannot reach the water

question.prompt: What happens at the end of The Thirsty Crow?
question.explanation: The pebbles raise the water and the crow drinks.

points: A story has a beginning, a middle and an end
The problem is in the middle and it is solved at the end
blocks.say: Let us remember. A story has a beginning, a middle and an end. The problem is in the middle, and it is solved at the end.

blocks.markdown:
A **prediction** is a clever guess about what will happen next.

Clues: dark grey clouds. Prediction: it will rain.
blocks.say: Good readers are clue detectives. A prediction is a clever guess about what will happen next. We use clues from the story and what we already know. If the sky turns dark and grey, what do you think will happen? Rain! The grey clouds were the clue.

scenes.caption: A sunny sky.
scenes.say: Here is a sunny sky. Everything is bright.

scenes.caption: Dark clouds are a clue.
scenes.say: Now the clouds are dark and grey. That is a clue. What will happen next?

scenes.caption: It rains.
scenes.say: Rain! We used the clue to make a prediction, and it came true.

question.prompt: Ali put on his swimming shorts and ran to the pool. What will probably happen next?
question.explanation: Swimming shorts are a clue that he is going swimming.

blocks.title: Predict the ending
materials: A grown-up to read with you
instructions: Read the book until the last few pages.
Stop and look at the clues in the pictures and words.
Say what you think will happen at the end.
Read on. Was your prediction right?
blocks.say: Now it is your turn to predict. Ask a grown-up to read you a picture book, but stop before the end. Use the clues to guess how it will finish, then read on and check.

blocks.alt: Clues in a story help us predict what happens next.
blocks.caption: Clues in a story help us predict what happens next.
blocks.say: Here are the clue detectives, magnifying glass at the ready.

blocks.answer_markdown: Yes! A prediction is a clever guess, so sometimes the story surprises us. That is part of the fun.
blocks.say: Here is a puzzle to think about. Can a prediction be wrong? Have a think, then tap to see.

blocks.markdown: Words **rhyme** when they end with the same sound: cat, hat, mat.
blocks.say: Poems love rhyme. Words rhyme when they end with the same sound. Cat and hat. Moon and spoon. Look at the ends of the words, not the beginnings. Listen: cat, hat, mat, sat. They all end with at. Let's watch rhyming words come together.

scenes.caption: cat and hat rhyme
scenes.say: And here is a hat. Cat and hat end with the same sound, at. They rhyme!

question.explanation: Moon and spoon both end in oon.

blocks.text: Stop 2: Rhythm and a brain game

blocks.markdown: **Rhythm** is the beat of a poem. Clap along to feel it.
blocks.say: A poem also has rhythm, which is its beat. Clap along as you say it: Twinkle, twinkle, little star. Each clap is one beat. Then play the memory game and listen out for the beat.

question.prompt: What is rhythm in a poem?
question.explanation: Rhythm is the beat of a poem.

points: Rhyming words end with the same sound
Rhythm is the beat of a poem
blocks.say: Let us remember. Rhyming words end with the same sound. Rhythm is the beat.

terms.meaning: Words that end with the same sound, like cat and hat.
The beat of a poem or song.
A short piece of writing, often with rhyme and rhythm.

blocks.markdown: To write a poem: choose a topic, find rhyming words, write four lines, read it aloud.
blocks.say: You can write a poem too! Here is a plan. First, choose a topic, like a cat. Then think of rhyming words, like cat and hat. Then write four short lines. Finally, read it aloud to hear the rhythm. Watch the steps.

scenes.caption: Choose a topic.
scenes.say: Step one. Choose a topic. We choose a cat.

scenes.caption: Find rhyming words.
scenes.say: Step two. Think of rhyming words. Cat, hat, mat.

scenes.caption: Write four lines.
scenes.say: Step three. Write the lines. Little cat on the mat, wearing a tiny hat.

blocks.title: My four-line poem
instructions: Think of two pairs of rhyming words.
Write four short lines that end with your rhymes.
Read it aloud, clapping the beat.
blocks.say: Time to write your own. Pick a topic you love, find two rhyming pairs, and write four lines. Read it to someone at home.
